edges.description: Fragmented mitochondria cannot be efficiently transported along axons, as mitofusin-2 also plays a direct role in mitochondrial motility and attachment to motor proteins.
Failure of mitochondrial delivery to distal axon terminals causes energy failure and triggers length-dependent axonal degeneration.
Disrupted neurofilament network impairs axonal caliber and slow axonal transport, contributing to axonal degeneration.
Defective endosomal trafficking impairs neurotrophin receptor signaling and autophagy, leading to sensory axon degeneration.
Persistent disruption of neurotrophin signaling endosome transport deprives long axons of trophic support and contributes to distal axonal degeneration.

edges.description: Sorbitol accumulation and polyol-pathway dysfunction contribute to the length-dependent peripheral axon degeneration seen in SORD-CMT2.

Sequestration of neurofilament and dynactin subunits into mutant small-heat-shock-protein aggregates removes components required for axonal structure and transport, and mutant HSPB8 degenerates neurites directly.
Reduced tRNA charging in long peripheral neurons is followed by distal-predominant axonal degeneration, with the central nervous system spared.
Failure of autophagic and lysosomal clearance in long neurons is followed by axonal and motor neuron degeneration.
Absence of lamin A/C is followed by axonal loss and enlargement in peripheral nerve.
Reduced mitochondrial energy output leaves the longest peripheral axons, which have the largest transport and metabolic demand, unable to sustain their distal segments.
Biallelic MPV17 variants can produce a pure axonal sensorimotor neuropathy, with none of the hepatic or cerebral disease the same gene causes in its depletion-syndrome presentation.
Loss of control over mitochondrial network dynamics compromises the function of myelinated peripheral nerve and contributes to the axonal degeneration of CMT2K.
A weakened axonal sodium-potassium pump is proposed as a degenerative pathway in peripheral nerve axons and a candidate therapeutic target.
Loss of the CADM3-CADM4 adhesion pairing disorganizes the myelinated axon and converges on the shared length-dependent axonal degeneration of CMT2.
Reduced Jagged1 availability at the cell surface compromises peripheral nerve integrity, particularly of the recurrent laryngeal nerve, and converges on the shared axonal degeneration of CMT2.

Reduced KCC3 cotransport precedes the length-dependent sensorimotor neuropathy seen in these patients; the intervening steps are not established, so the link is recorded as indirect with unknown intermediates.
Failure to inactivate RhoA disrupts axonal and synaptic morphology in motor neurons, converging on the shared motor-predominant axonal degeneration of this subtype.
Reduced complex IV assembly and activity produces a bioenergetic deficit in the axon and, in the fly model, progressive axonal degeneration of sensory neurons.
Partial loss of mitochondrial aspartyl-tRNA aminoacylation impairs mitochondrial function and converges on the length-dependent axonal degeneration seen in these individuals.

nodes.description: Cytoplasmic aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases charge tRNAs with their amino acid. Dominant CMT2 alleles of AARS1 (CMT2N) and MARS1 (CMT2U) behave as loss-of-function in aminoacylation and yeast complementation assays, and the resulting peripheral phenotype is a length-dependent axonal degeneration without central features. The GARS1 disease CMT2D is modeled separately in this entry, because its alleles act through aberrant new interactions rather than through the charging deficit alone.

evidence.reference_title: A recurrent loss-of-function alanyl-tRNA synthetase (AARS) mutation in patients with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2N (CMT2N).

nodes.description: CADM3 is expressed on the axon and binds CADM4 on the myelinating Schwann cell; this pairing organizes the myelinated fibre at the axon-glia interface. The recurrent CMT2FF variant Tyr172Cys introduces a new disulphide bond, retains the mutant protein in the endoplasmic reticulum, reduces its surface expression and lowers its co-localization with CADM4 at intercellular contacts. Knock-in mice show normal nerve conduction and myelin morphology but disordered axonal organization, so the lesion is an adhesion and domain-organization defect in an otherwise normally myelinated axon rather than a demyelinating one.

evidence.reference_title: A CADM3 variant causes Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease with marked upper limb involvement.
evidence.snippet: In the peripheral nerve, axon-Schwann cell interaction is essential for the structural organization of myelinated fibres and is primarily mediated by the binding of CADM3, expressed in axons, to CADM4, expressed by myelinating Schwann cells.

evidence.reference_title: A CADM3 variant causes Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease with marked upper limb involvement.
evidence.snippet: Our data support a retention of the mutant protein in the endoplasmic reticulum and reduced cell surface expression in vitro.

evidence.reference_title: A CADM3 variant causes Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease with marked upper limb involvement.
evidence.snippet: Our findings indicate the involvement of abnormal axon-glia interaction as a disease-causing mechanism in CMT patients with CADM3 mutations.

nodes.description: ATP1A1 encodes the alpha-1 subunit of the Na+,K+-ATPase and is present on the axolemma of myelinated sensory and motor axons and at Schmidt-Lanterman incisures. Several CMT2DD substitutions reduce pump current in a heterologous expression system, pointing to a loss-of-function defect in the sodium-potassium pump.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in ATP1A1 Cause Dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth Type 2.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in ATP1A1 Cause Dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth Type 2.
evidence.snippet: demonstrated significant reduction in Na+ current activity in some, but not all, ouabain-insensitive ATP1A1 mutants, suggesting a loss-of-function defect of the Na+,K+ pump

evidence.reference_title: A CADM3 variant causes Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease with marked upper limb involvement.

evidence.reference_title: A CADM3 variant causes Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease with marked upper limb involvement.

evidence.snippet: Hypomorphic variants, such as p.Ser238Phe, when paired with more deleterious variants, result in isolated axonal CMT, whereas more severe combinations-although not as deleterious as those seen in leukoencephalopathy with brainstem and spinal cord involvement and lactate elevation-result in axonal CMT with central nervous system involvement, albeit without leukoencephalopathy.

evidence.reference_title: Ubiquitin ligase defect by DCAF8 mutation causes HMSN2 with giant axons.

evidence.snippet: in exon 8 of dehydrogenase E1 and transketolase domain-containing 1 (DHTKD1) in all eight affected individuals

nodes.description: The final common pathway in CMT2 involves dying-back degeneration of peripheral nerve axons. The longest axons are affected first due to their higher metabolic and transport demands, producing the characteristic length-dependent pattern of weakness and sensory loss. This is a Wallerian-like process distinct from neuronal apoptosis.

evidence.reference_title: Axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease: from Common Pathogenic Mechanisms to Emerging Treatment Opportunities.
evidence.snippet: Genetic neuropathies that primarily cause axonal degeneration, as opposed to demyelination, are most often classified as Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 (CMT2) and are the focus of this review.

evidence.reference_title: Mitofusin 2 Dysfunction and Disease in Mice and Men.
evidence.snippet: the challenge of defining the central underlying mechanism(s) linking mitochondrial abnormalities to progressive dying-back of peripheral arm and leg nerves in CMT2A is largely unmet

evidence.snippet: All patients presented with distal weakness and atrophy in the lower limb, two of whom had minor clinical sensory abnormalities and small fiber neuropathy.

evidence.reference_title: Axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease: from Common Pathogenic Mechanisms to Emerging Treatment Opportunities.
evidence.snippet: Inherited peripheral neuropathies are a genetically and phenotypically diverse group of disorders that lead to degeneration of peripheral neurons with resulting sensory and motor dysfunction.

evidence.snippet: It is characterised by prominent sensory loss, often complicated by severe ulcero-mutilations of toes or feet, and variable motor involvement.

nodes.description: Fragmented mitochondria resulting from MFN2 dysfunction fail to be efficiently transported to distal axon terminals. MFN2 also directly regulates mitochondrial transport by interacting with the Miro/Milton motor adaptor complex. Energy deficits at distal terminals result from inadequate mitochondrial delivery.

nodes.description: MPV17 is an inner mitochondrial membrane protein serving mitochondrial deoxynucleotide homeostasis. Biallelic MPV17 variants were first described in a mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome with early-onset liver failure, and can also present as an isolated axonal sensorimotor neuropathy with no liver or brain involvement, which is CMT2EE.

evidence.reference_title: MPV17 mutations in juvenile- and adult-onset axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy.
evidence.snippet: MPV17 encodes a putative channel-forming protein of the inner mitochondrial membrane and is involved in mitochondrial deoxynucleotide homeostasis.

evidence.reference_title: MPV17 mutations in juvenile- and adult-onset axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy.
evidence.snippet: Here, we describe five additional patients from two unrelated families with sensorimotor axonal neuropathy without hepatocerebral affection caused by homozygous MPV17 variants.

nodes.description: GDAP1 sits in the mitochondrial outer membrane and drives fission of the mitochondrial network. CMT-associated truncations fail to reach mitochondria and lose fragmentation activity, and point mutations reduce it strongly, so the GDAP1 defect is a loss of fission rather than the loss of fusion produced by MFN2. Both leave the mitochondrial network mishandled, which is why GDAP1 is wired to its own node rather than to Mitochondrial Fragmentation.

evidence.reference_title: Ganglioside-induced differentiation associated protein 1 is a regulator of the mitochondrial network: new implications for Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.
evidence.snippet: GDAP1 truncations that are found in patients who have CMT are not targeted to mitochondria and have lost mitochondrial fragmentation activity.

evidence.reference_title: Ganglioside-induced differentiation associated protein 1 is a regulator of the mitochondrial network: new implications for Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.
evidence.snippet: GDAP1 is located in the mitochondrial outer membrane and regulates the mitochondrial network.

One reported variant reduced DARS2 enzymatic activity by 75 percent in HEK293 cells.

nodes.description: COX18 translocates the C-terminal tail of MTCO2 across the mitochondrial inner membrane during assembly of respiratory chain complex IV. The reported CMT2MM splice variant produces a stable but defective COX18 isoform lacking exon 2, which impairs complex IV assembly and activity and lowers the mitochondrial membrane potential. This is a primary respiratory-chain lesion, distinct from the mitochondrial-dynamics lesions of MFN2 and GDAP1 curated above.

nodes.description: The axonal neurofilament network is disrupted in several CMT2 subtypes, by mutation of a neurofilament subunit or by loss of the ubiquitin ligases that turn neurofilaments over. NEFL mutations cause abnormal neurofilament assembly and accumulation of neurofilament aggregates in neuronal cell bodies and proximal axons. Disrupted neurofilament stoichiometry impairs axonal caliber maintenance and reduces neurofilament density in myelinated axons, particularly affecting large-caliber fibers. NEFH frameshift alleles that read through into the 3' UTR append a cryptic amyloidogenic element, and the resulting protein aggregates. Loss of TRIM2 or weakened assembly of the Cullin-4 ligase complex through DCAF8 removes the degradation arm instead, so neurofilaments accumulate inside axons and, for DCAF8, produce the giant axons that name GAN2.

evidence.reference_title: Effects of Charcot-Marie-Tooth-linked mutations of the neurofilament light subunit on intermediate filament formation.
evidence.snippet: Both mutations disrupted the self-assembly of human NFL.

evidence.reference_title: Allele-Specific Gene Editing Rescues Pathology in a Human Model of Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type 2E.
evidence.snippet: Diseased motor neurons recapitulated known pathologic phenotypes at early time points of differentiation, including aberrant accumulation of neurofilament light chain protein in neuronal cell bodies.

evidence.reference_title: Myelinated axons fail to develop properly in a genetically authentic mouse model of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2E.
evidence.snippet: the p.N98S mutation causes a profound reduction of neurofilaments in the myelinated axons of the PNS and CNS, resulting in substantially reduced axonal diameters, particularly of large myelinated axons, and distal axon loss in the PNS.

evidence.reference_title: Cryptic amyloidogenic elements in mutant NEFH causing Charcot-Marie-Tooth 2 trigger aggresome formation and neuronal death.
evidence.snippet: Consistently, we show that these mutations cause protein aggregation which are recognised by the autophagic pathway in motoneurons and triggered caspase 3 activation leading to apoptosis in neuroblastoma cells.

evidence.reference_title: Deficiency of the E3 ubiquitin ligase TRIM2 in early-onset axonal neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: Trim2-gene trap mice showed axonopathy with accumulations of neurofilaments inside axons.

evidence.reference_title: Deficiency of the E3 ubiquitin ligase TRIM2 in early-onset axonal neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: TRIM2 is an E3 ubiquitin ligase that ubiquitinates neurofilament light chain, a component of the intermediate filament in axons.

evidence.reference_title: Ubiquitin ligase defect by DCAF8 mutation causes HMSN2 with giant axons.
evidence.snippet: This mutation results in decreased DDB1-DCAF8 association, leading to an E3 ubiquitin ligase defect that is likely associated with neurofilament degradation.

evidence.reference_title: Ubiquitin ligase defect by DCAF8 mutation causes HMSN2 with giant axons.
evidence.snippet: Giant axons with neurofilament accumulations were found in 3 affected persons who had undergone nerve biopsy evaluations.

nodes.description: Lamin A/C is a component of the nuclear envelope. A homozygous LMNA founder allele causes autosomal recessive axonal CMT2B1, and sciatic nerves of lamin-A/C-null mice show the loss of axons, axonal enlargement and unmyelinated profiles seen in human peripheral axonopathy.

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous defects in LMNA, encoding lamin A/C nuclear-envelope proteins, cause autosomal recessive axonal neuropathy in human (Charcot-Marie-Tooth disorder type 2) and mouse.
evidence.snippet: The finding of site-specific amino acid substitutions in limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 1B, autosomal dominant Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy, dilated cardiomyopathy type 1A, autosomal dominant partial lipodystrophy, and, now, AR-CMT2 suggests the existence of distinct functional domains

evidence.reference_title: Human Rab7 mutation mimics features of Charcot-Marie-Tooth neuropathy type 2B in Drosophila.
evidence.snippet: Missense mutations in RAB7A, the gene encoding the small GTPase Rab7, cause CMT2B and increase Rab7 activity.

evidence.reference_title: RAB7A / Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 (Definitive)
evidence.snippet: RAB7A | HGNC:9788 | Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 | MONDO:0018993 | AD | Definitive

nodes.description: Absent or reduced deep tendon reflexes, particularly at the ankles, reflecting loss of the afferent sensory arc.

JAG1 encodes the canonical Notch ligand Jagged1. The two reported CMT2HH missense variants (p.Ser577Arg, p.Ser650Pro) impair post-translational glycosylation of the protein and reduce the amount of JAG1 reaching the cell surface, where it would otherwise engage Notch receptors on neighbouring cells. Mice heterozygous for the CMT2-associated alleles develop mild peripheral neuropathy.

evidence.reference_title: Dominant mutations of the Notch ligand Jagged1 cause peripheral neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: Our studies of mutant protein posttranslational modification and localization indicated that the mutations (p.Ser577Arg, p.Ser650Pro) impair protein glycosylation and reduce JAG1 cell surface expression.

evidence.reference_title: Dominant mutations of the Notch ligand Jagged1 cause peripheral neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: Mice harboring heterozygous CMT2-associated mutations exhibited mild peripheral neuropathy, and homozygous expression resulted in embryonic lethality by midgestation.

nodes.description: SLC12A6 encodes KCC3, a potassium-chloride cotransporter. Dominantly acting de novo missense variants reduce potassium influx through the mutant cotransporter when expressed in Xenopus oocytes. How reduced KCC3 transport injures the peripheral nerve is not established; the largest dominant SLC12A6 cohort states that more work is needed to understand the mechanism, and this node therefore records the measured transport deficit rather than a downstream nerve mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: De novo variants in SLC12A6 cause sporadic early-onset progressive sensorimotor neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: Modelling of the mutant KCC3 cotransporter in Xenopus oocytes showed a significant reduction in potassium influx for both changes.

evidence.reference_title: De novo variants in SLC12A6 cause sporadic early-onset progressive sensorimotor neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: We identified heterozygous de novo variants in SLC12A6 in three unrelated patients with intermediate CMT.

evidence.reference_title: Spectrum of dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease due to SLC12A6 variants.
evidence.snippet: Twenty-three individuals from 13 families carried nine variants classified either as pathogenic/likely pathogenic or variants of uncertain significance segregating in multiple family members, including five novel variants.

evidence.reference_title: Spectrum of dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease due to SLC12A6 variants.
evidence.snippet: Clinical phenotype varied dramatically with genotype; Arg207His and Ser647Pro caused a severe childhood-onset, sensory and motor, conduction-slowing neuropathy, whereas Gly552Asp caused a mild, adult-onset, sensory-predominant neuropathy, Thr991Ala an infantile-onset motor neuropathy, and the Met282Lys/Gly286Cys locus a complex, axonal neuropathy.

evidence.reference_title: De novo variants in SLC12A6 cause sporadic early-onset progressive sensorimotor neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: Our findings expand the genotypic and phenotypic spectrum associated with SLC12A6 variants from autosomal-recessive HMSN/ACC to dominant-acting de novo variants causing a milder clinical presentation with early-onset neuropathy.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic mutations in SORD cause a common and potentially treatable hereditary neuropathy with implications for diabetes.
evidence.snippet: Here we report biallelic mutations in the sorbitol dehydrogenase gene (SORD) as the most frequent recessive form of hereditary neuropathy.

nodes.description: Biallelic SORD loss-of-function variants reduce sorbitol dehydrogenase activity in the polyol pathway. Loss of SORD protein causes intracellular and serum sorbitol accumulation, which is linked to peripheral axon degeneration in patient cells and Drosophila models.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic mutations in SORD cause a common and potentially treatable hereditary neuropathy with implications for diabetes.
evidence.snippet: In patient-derived fibroblasts, we found a complete loss of SORD protein and increased intracellular sorbitol.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic mutations in SORD cause a common and potentially treatable hereditary neuropathy with implications for diabetes.
evidence.snippet: In Drosophila, loss of SORD orthologs caused synaptic degeneration and progressive motor impairment.

evidence.reference_title: ALS5/SPG11/KIAA1840 mutations cause autosomal recessive axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.
evidence.snippet: Interestingly, we identified 15 ALS5/SPG11/KIAA1840 mutations in 12 families

nodes.description: Mutations in the alpha-crystallin domain of the small heat-shock proteins HSPB1 (HSP27) and HSPB8 (HSP22) convert them from chaperones into aggregation-prone proteins. Mutant HSP27 forms insoluble intracellular aggregates that sequester neurofilament middle chain and the p150 subunit of dynactin, and mutant HSP22 degenerates neurites selectively in motor neurons while leaving sensory and cortical neurons and glial cells largely unaffected. Alleles of both genes are reported in axonal CMT2 and in distal hereditary motor neuropathy.

evidence.reference_title: A mutation in the small heat-shock protein HSPB1 leading to distal hereditary motor neuronopathy disrupts neurofilament assembly and the axonal transport of specific cellular cargoes.
evidence.snippet: Mutant (P182L) but not wild-type HSPB1 led to the formation of insoluble intracellular aggregates and to the sequestration in the cytoplasm of selective cellular components, including neurofilament middle chain subunit (NF-M) and p150 dynactin.

evidence.reference_title: Mutant HSPB8 causes motor neuron-specific neurite degeneration.
evidence.snippet: In motor neurons, expression of both HSPB8 K141N and K141E mutations clearly resulted in neurite degeneration

nodes.description: Characteristic high-stepping gait due to foot drop from peroneal muscle weakness, requiring exaggerated hip and knee flexion during the swing phase of walking.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Characteristics of Gait Disturbance in Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease and Future Directions in Physical Therapy.
evidence.snippet: One of the hallmark manifestations of CMT is gait disturbance. As the disease progresses, individuals often develop foot drop and foot deformities such as pes cavus and equinus, leading to a significant decline in gait function.

evidence.reference_title: Deficiency of the E3 ubiquitin ligase TRIM2 in early-onset axonal neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: We show that the patient fibroblasts are practically devoid of TRIM2, through mRNA and protein instability caused by the mutations.

evidence.reference_title: A novel mutation in VCP causes Charcot-Marie-Tooth Type 2 disease.
evidence.snippet: We identified a novel VCP mutation (p.Glu185Lys) segregating in an autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 family.
